messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: RStan install 404 warnings?
parts:
More than one user has reported off list that there
are problems with 404 warnings installing RStan 1.2.0,
which look as follows

> install.packages('rstan', type = 'source')
> Warning in install.packages :
> cannot open: HTTP status was '404 Not Found'
...

Despite the warning, RStan 1.2.0 seems to install and run
OK.

I'm not an R expert, so I'm just posting this to our
lists in the hope that somebody can diagnose the issue.

Users have reported this using Windows 7 and Mac OS X.

I did not get the warnings when I installed it.

- Bob

On Fri, Mar 8, 2013 at 12:49 AM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
More than one user has reported off list that there
are problems with 404 warnings installing RStan 1.2.0,
which look as follows

> install.packages('rstan', type = 'source')
> Warning in install.packages :
>    cannot open: HTTP status was '404 Not Found'

This appears to be an RStudio only thing because it overwrites the install.packages function with

> install.packages
function(...) .rs.callAs(name,
                                                             hook,
                                                             original,
                                                             ...)
<environment: 0x3ac9a70>
> .rs.callAs
function(name, f, ...)
{
   # TODO: figure out how to print the args (...) as part of the message
   
   # run the original function (f). setup condition handlers soley so that
   # we can correctly print the name of the function called in error
   # and warning messages -- otherwise R prints "original(...)"
   withCallingHandlers(tryCatch(f(...),
                                error=function(e)
                                {
                                   cat("Error in ", name, " : ", e$message,
                                       " ", sep="")
                                }),
                       warning=function(w)
                       {
                          cat("Warning in ", name, " :  ",  w$message,
                              " ", sep="")
                          invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
                       })
}
<environment: 0x374e908>

And I imagine the invokeRestart() explains why it subsequently installs. I would guess it is just a flaky internet connection or flaky server thing.

Ben

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] RStan install 404 warnings?
parts: I still cannot reproduce this problem with the Rstudio version 0.97.306 on Mac.  But I do not think it is a problem due to flaky internet connection or server.  From previous output (copied here):

> install.packages("rstan", type = "source")
Warning in install.packages :
  cannot open: HTTP status was '404 Not Found'
Warning in install.packages :
  cannot open: HTTP status was '404 Not Found'

Warning in install.packages :
  unable to access index for repository http://wiki.stan.googlecode.com/git/R/bin/macosx/leopard/contrib/2.15

install.packages() tries to access the binary version of rstan in the repository we defined and of course it cannot two files (namely PACKAGE.gz or PACKAGE).  The problem is that it should never try to look for those files since we specify type='source'.  The good thing is that after failing to find the binary version, it looks for the source and then it works.  

From the code (http://tinyurl.com/aqpguxs) where RStudio overwrites the install.packages function, I cannot figure out why this would happen. 

--
Jiqiang
